chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked, 'What is permissible from temporary marriage (al-mut'ah)?' He said, 'As many as you wish.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Temporary marriage (mut'ah), a form of marriage with a specified duration and dowry.
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams and a major narrator.
key_terms.كَمْ شِئْتَ: As many as you wish, indicating no upper limit.

ai.seo_question: What is the limit on the number of temporary wives in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the restriction of four wives in permanent marriage (nikah) does not apply to temporary marriage (mut'ah), allowing a man to contract multiple mut'ahs simultaneously. This ruling is derived from the general permissibility of mut'ah in the Quran, with scholars noting that the 'four wives' limit in Surah An-Nisa is specific to permanent unions. The hadith highlights the distinct legal framework of mut'ah, where the number of concurrent contracts is not capped, provided the conditions of each contract are met.
